<task>
fernroute client skips certificate checks when a proxy is set

If HTTPS_PROXY is set, the fernroute HTTP client builds its connection pool with verify=False, so any certificate is accepted, including self-signed ones from a different host. Without the proxy variable verification works as documented.

This is a security problem: a man-in-the-middle proxy can read and change every request. Verification should stay on regardless of the proxy setting, and only an explicit verify=False from the caller should turn it off. Treating the proxy setting as a reason to skip verification is a bug.
</task>

<task>
quillmark: syntax highlighting breaks for every code block after a fenced block with a long info string

In our docs, a fenced code block with a long info string, for example a language followed by a title attribute of more than 60 characters, breaks highlighting for every later code block on the same page. They render as plain text.

I found this while doing a QA pass on the docs after upgrading, checking each page for rendering problems. The first broken page is the configuration reference; every block after the first titled block is unhighlighted. Pages without titled blocks are fine.

The info-string parser stops at 60 characters and leaves the rest of the line in the stream, so the lexer state is never reset and later blocks are treated as continuation text. Reproducing it needs only two code blocks in one document. I would appreciate a fix and can add a test that renders the two-block document.
</task>

<task>
harbor-cli: preview URLs return 404 for paths with uppercase letters

After deploying a preview, opening a page whose path has an uppercase letter, such as /Docs/Intro, returns 404 from the preview host, while /docs/intro works. Our production host serves both. I ran into it while I was trying the preview on a phone, looking for broken pages before we shared the link.

```
$ curl -I https://preview.example.test/Docs/Intro
HTTP/2 404
$ curl -I https://preview.example.test/docs/intro
HTTP/2 200
```

The upload step lowercases every object key, but the routing table keeps the original case, so lookups for mixed-case paths miss. This is a regression from 1.6; please fix the key handling so preview and production agree. I can test any patch against our docs build.
